    largest = max(sizes, key=sizes.__getitem__, default=None)
    if largest is None or sizes[largest] <= 1024:
        return False
    if largest in ("stdout", "stderr"):
        text = str(parts[largest])
        keep = len(text) // 4
        marker = f"\n[… {len(text) - 2 * keep} characters omitted to fit the result …]\n"
        shorter = text[:keep] + marker + text[len(text) - keep :]
        result[largest] = {**result[largest], "text": shorter, "truncated": True}
    elif largest == "outputs":
        outputs = cast(list[Message], parts[largest])
        kept = outputs[: len(outputs) // 2]
        note = f"[{len(outputs) - len(kept)} outputs omitted to fit the result]"
        result["outputs"] = [*kept, {"type": "display", "data": {"text/plain": note}}]
    elif largest == "traceback":
        lines = cast(list[str], parts[largest])
        shorter = (
            lines[len(lines) // 2 :] if len(lines) > 1 else [bounded(lines[0], len(lines[0]) // 2)]
        )
        result["error"] = {**result["error"], "traceback": shorter}
    else:
        files = cast(list[str], parts[largest])
        result["written_files"] = files[: len(files) // 2]
        result["written_files_truncated"] = True
    return True


def _item(container: object, key: str) -> object:
    return cast(Message, container).get(key) if isinstance(container, dict) else None


async def serve_stdio(
    root: Path,
    *,
    subreaper: bool = False,
    protected: bool = False,
    kernel_idle: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Serve one connection on stdin and stdout until stdin closes."""
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    # Keep the protocol on its own descriptor; anything else printing to stdout
    # (a library, a kernel's launcher) goes to stderr instead.
    protocol_fd = os.dup(1)
    os.dup2(2, 1)
    reader = asyncio.StreamReader(limit=MAX_REQUEST)
    await loop.connect_read_pipe(lambda: asyncio.StreamReaderProtocol(reader), sys.stdin)
    transport, protocol = await loop.connect_write_pipe(
        asyncio.streams.FlowControlMixin, os.fdopen(protocol_fd, "wb", buffering=0)
    )
    writer = asyncio.StreamWriter(transport, protocol, None, loop)
    lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def send(message: Message) -> None:
        line = fit_line(message)
        if line is None:
            print("executor: dropped an event too large to send", file=sys.stderr)
            return
        async with lock:
            writer.write(line)
            await writer.drain()

    executor = Executor(
        root, send, subreaper=subreaper, protected=protected, kernel_idle=kernel_idle
    )
    if kernel_idle is not None:
        executor.reaper = executor.spawn(executor.reap_idle_kernels(kernel_idle))
    try:
        while True:
            try:
                line = await reader.readline()
            except ValueError:  # a request over MAX_REQUEST, already discarded
                continue
            if not line:
                break
            try:
                request = json.loads(line)
            except (ValueError, RecursionError):
                await send(
                    {
                        "type": "reply",
                        "id": None,
                        "ok": False,
                        "error": {"kind": "invalid_request", "message": "not JSON"},
                    }
                )
                continue
            if not isinstance(request, dict):
                continue
            executor.spawn(executor.handle(cast(Message, request)))
    finally:
        await executor.shutdown()
        with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
            writer.close()


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Sandbox Science executor")
    parser.add_argument("--stdio", action="store_true", required=True, help="serve on stdin/stdout")
    parser.add_argument("--root", required=True, type=Path, help="project directory")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--kernel-idle", type=float, default=None, help="stop kernels unused this many seconds"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root: Path = args.root
    root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    state = root / ".executor"
    (state / "runtime").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (root / SHARED).mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    (state / "ipython").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    os.environ.setdefault("JUPYTER_RUNTIME_DIR", str(state / "runtime"))
    os.environ.setdefault("IPYTHONDIR", str(state / "ipython"))
    protected = protect_process()
    # A subreaper adopts its descendants' orphans, so leftovers stay findable below it.
    subreaper = _prctl(PR_SET_CHILD_SUBREAPER, 1)
    idle: float | None = args.kernel_idle
    if idle is not None and not idle > 0:
        parser.error("--kernel-idle must be a positive number of seconds")
    asyncio.run(
        serve_stdio(root.resolve(), subreaper=subreaper, protected=protected, kernel_idle=idle)
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Corrected dispatcher lifecycle review checklist

Pending exact immutable checkpoint/signed clean freeze. This is a source-review
checklist, not source or runtime clearance. Preserve the early37case record and
its original findings/probes.

1. Recheck L1's same400k-NUL malformed-language probe against exact corrected
   metadata preflight, including copied scalar negatives before encoding/equality.
   Avoid rerunning unrelated gate suites.
2. Recheck L2's retainedlast5/birth1 and rememberedbirth2 contradictions. Every
   selected birth/generation pair must agree before certification or mutation;
   wrong/missing pairs hold/refuse. Input birth/info generation must agree too.
3. Recheck C1's distinct old-open/current-new fake channel. The actual selected
   channel must match fresh proof before sending cancellation. Keep production
   reachability of the old constructed state explicitly unproven.
4. Public manager.cancel must retain legacy behavior while refusing selected-child
   identities, including terminal/retained records and stale/missing live flags.
   Exact project scoping must precede disclosure. Corrupt/missing original marker
   or envelope must never downgrade into MAIN cancellation.
5. The private selected-child path must require original binding, execution and
   attempt, and use the actual original owned channel. Wrong child/attempt/channel
   must refuse without touching parent/sibling cancellation or sending a cancel.
6. Watchdog, timeout, overflow, recovery and shutdown paths must continue to cancel
   their own original attempt through the private owner. They must not accidentally
   hit public selected-child refusal, reconstruct selection from current state,
   cancel another child, or silently lose cleanup after repeated caller cancellation.
7. Whole-session close remains an intentional owner of legacy and child kernels.
   It persists eligibility withdrawal before cleanup, invalidates selected observer
   tokens and drains actual admitted child work. This is not a blanket refusal of
   public session lifecycle operations.
8. Preserve child maps/IDs/raw-normalized generation/birth, legacy-only listings,
   actual-launch/close fences and same shared passive global8/per-environment1 lane.
   Reuse the source-identical parts of the37prior fake cases; rerun changed seams.
9. Distinguish exact signed source clearance from future combined full gates,
   helper/admission review and real OpenShell acceptance. Lab33 borrows the single
   manager.run_dispatcher and its owned drain; no helper activation here.

Allowed review execution: exact AST, pure typed DTOs, cooperative fake kernel/
channel/async owner probes only. No actual research kernel, service, VM, RPC/HTTP,
model/provider, private file/hash, publication, repository mutation or broad suite.

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
"""Internal original-run dispatch; no route, launcher, tool or caller authentication."""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import hashlib
import json
import re
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Literal, cast

from pydantic import ValidationError

from sandbox_science.contracts import (
    TERMINAL_STATES,
    ErrorKind,
    Execution,
    ExecutionContext,
    ExecutionState,
    KernelInfo,
    KernelLineageEntry,
    KernelStatusRequest,
    new_id,
)
from sandbox_science.contracts.kernel_lineage import KernelBirthPin
from sandbox_science.contracts.run_cells import (
    RunCellExecution,
    RunCellRequest,
    RunKernelObservation,
    run_cell_bytes,
)
from sandbox_science.contracts.run_kernels import (
    RunKernelBinding,
    checked_run_kernel_binding,
    run_kernel_binding_sha256,
)

from .errors import WorkerError
from .run_kernel_state import RunControlReceipt, unavailable
from .run_kernels import RunKernelBindings

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .channel import ExecutorChannel
    from .manager import ExecutionManager, _Environment, _Live

# This internal component deliberately composes the existing Manager lifetime.
# pyright: reportPrivateUsage=false


def _context(binding: RunKernelBinding) -> ExecutionContext:
    return ExecutionContext(
        project_id=binding.scope.project_id,
        session_id=binding.scope.session_id,
        environment_id=binding.scope.environment_id,
    )


def _wire(binding: RunKernelBinding) -> dict[str, object]:
    return {
        "run_binding": binding.model_dump(mode="json"),
        "run_binding_sha256": run_kernel_binding_sha256(binding),
    }


class RunKernelDispatcher:
    """Requires explicitly supplied controller admission; never manufactures it.

    Effects use only the original already-connected managed channel. Completed
    controls replay historical receipts; pending unknown effects are never resent.
    """

    def __init__(self, manager: ExecutionManager) -> None:
        self.manager = manager
        self.state = manager.store.run_kernel_state
        self.bindings = RunKernelBindings(manager.store)
        self._controls: dict[str, asyncio.Task[RunControlReceipt]] = {}

    def initialize(self) -> None:
        self.state.initialize()

    def proof(
        self, binding: RunKernelBinding, *, recovery: bool = False, allow_closed: bool = False
    ) -> tuple[_Environment, ExecutorChannel]:
        binding = checked_run_kernel_binding(binding)
        m, scope = self.manager, binding.scope
        env = m._environments.get(scope.environment_id)
        channel = env.channel if env is not None else None
        if (
            m._closing
            or env is None
            or channel is None
            or channel.closed
            or channel.detaching
            or env.lock.locked()
            or scope.environment_id in m._daemon_fences
            or scope.environment_id in m._quarantined
            or scope.environment_id in m._released_environments
            or (not recovery and scope.environment_id in m._recovering)
            or (scope.project_id, scope.environment_id, scope.session_id) in m._closing_sessions
            or m.store.recycle_needed(scope.environment_id)
        ):
            raise unavailable()
        if (
            channel.daemon_token is None
            or channel.incarnation != binding.incarnation
            or type(channel.hello.get("run_kernel_protocol")) is not int
            or channel.hello.get("run_kernel_protocol") != 1
        ):
            raise unavailable()
        expected = (binding.incarnation, binding.sandbox, binding.sandbox_id)
        identity = m.daemon_identity(scope.environment_id) if m.daemon_identity else None
        if (
            type(identity) is not tuple
            or len(identity) != 2
            or any(type(item) is not str for item in identity)
            or identity != (binding.sandbox, binding.sandbox_id)
            or self.bindings.endpoint(scope.environment_id) != expected
            or self.bindings.get(scope).binding != binding
        ):
            raise unavailable()
        if not allow_closed and self.state.closed(binding):
            raise unavailable()
        return env, channel

    def check(
        self,
        binding: RunKernelBinding,
        environment: _Environment,
        channel: ExecutorChannel,
        *,
        recovery: bool = False,
        allow_closed: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        current = self.proof(binding, recovery=recovery, allow_closed=allow_closed)
        if current[0] is not environment or current[1] is not channel:
            raise unavailable()

    @staticmethod
    def admission(admitted: Callable[[], bool]) -> None:
        if not callable(admitted) or admitted() is not True:
            raise unavailable()

    async def submit(
        self, request: RunCellRequest, *, admitted: Callable[[], bool]
    ) -> tuple[RunCellExecution, bool]:
        try:
            raw = run_cell_bytes(request)
            request = RunCellRequest.model_validate_json(raw, strict=True)
        except (ValueError, TypeError, UnicodeError, ValidationError):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.INVALID_REQUEST, "invalid internal child request") from None
        m = self.manager
        self.admission(admitted)
        found = m.store.run_operation(request.context.project_id, request.operation_id)
        if found is not None:
            execution_id, digest = found
            if digest != hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest():
                raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.CONFLICT, "internal child operation already differs")
            execution = m.store.run_execution(execution_id)
            saved = self.state.request(execution)
            if saved != request:
                raise unavailable()
            return self.wrap(request.binding, execution), False
        environment, channel = self.proof(request.binding)
        m._package_origin(request.cell(), None)
        execution = Execution(
            execution_id=new_id("exe"),
            attempt_id=new_id("att"),
            operation_id=request.operation_id,
            kind="cell",
            context=request.context,
            state=ExecutionState.QUEUED,
            submitted_at=datetime.now(UTC),
        )

        def validate() -> None:
            self.admission(admitted)
            self.check(request.binding, environment, channel)

        m.store.insert_run_execution(execution, request, validate=validate)
        live = m._track(execution, request.output_limit_bytes)
        live.is_run, live.run_request, live.run_admission = True, request, admitted
        m._state(live, ExecutionState.QUEUED)
        m.store.update_execution(live.execution)
        try:
            validate()
        except WorkerError:
            m._lose(live, "the original child channel before dispatch")
            raise
        m._spawn(m._dispatch(live, request))
        return self.wrap(request.binding, live.execution), True

    @staticmethod
    def wrap(binding: RunKernelBinding, execution: Execution) -> RunCellExecution:
        return RunCellExecution(
            binding=binding, binding_sha256=run_kernel_binding_sha256(binding), execution=execution
        )

    def get(
        self, binding: RunKernelBinding, execution_id: str, attempt_id: str
    ) -> RunCellExecution:
        binding = checked_run_kernel_binding(binding)
        if (
            type(execution_id) is not str
            or re.fullmatch(r"exe-[0-9a-f]{24}", execution_id) is None
            or type(attempt_id) is not str
            or re.fullmatch(r"att-[0-9a-f]{24}", attempt_id) is None
        ):
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.INVALID_REQUEST, "invalid original child attempt")
        execution = self.manager.store.run_execution(execution_id)
        request = self.state.request(execution)
        if execution.attempt_id != attempt_id or request.binding != binding:
            raise WorkerError(ErrorKind.NOT_FOUND, "no selected child attempt")
        return self.wrap(binding, execution)

    async def cancel(
        self,
        binding: RunKernelBinding,
        execution_id: str,
        attempt_id: str,
        *,
        admitted: Callable[[], bool],
    ) -> RunCellExecution:
        self.admission(admitted)
        result = self.get(binding, execution_id, attempt_id)
        if result.execution.state not in TERMINAL_STATES:
            self.proof(binding, allow_closed=True)
            await self.manager.cancel(execution_id)
        return self.get(binding, execution_id, attempt_id)

    def kernel(
        self,
        live: _Live,
        raw: object,
        *,
        remember: bool = False,
        restarted: bool = False,
        fingerprint: object = None,
    ) -> tuple[KernelInfo | None, bool]:
        request = live.run_request
        if request is None:
            return None, live.execution.kernel_state_lost
        try:
            info = self.map_kernel(
                request.binding,
                raw,
                live.channel,
                remember=remember,
                owning_execution=live.execution.execution_id if not live.reattached else None,
                restarted=restarted,
                fingerprint=fingerprint,
            )
        except (WorkerError, ValueError, ValidationError):
            if remember:
                raise
            return None, live.execution.kernel_state_lost
        return info, live.execution.kernel_state_lost or (
            type(raw) is dict and cast(dict[str, object], raw).get("state_lost") is True
        )

    def map_kernel(
        self,
        binding: RunKernelBinding,
        raw: object,
        channel: ExecutorChannel | None,
        *,
        remember: bool = False,
        owning_execution: str | None = None,
        restarted: bool = False,
        fingerprint: object = None,
    ) -> KernelInfo:
        environment, current_channel = self.proof(binding, recovery=True, allow_closed=True)
        del environment
        if current_channel is not channel or type(raw) is not dict:
            raise unavailable()
        raw = cast(dict[str, object], raw)
        generation, language, kernel_id = (
            raw.get("generation"),
            raw.get("language"),
            raw.get("kernel_id"),
        )
        binding_key = raw.get("run_binding_sha256")
        birth_id = raw.get("birth_id")
        if (
            type(binding_key) is not str
            or len(binding_key) != 64
            or type(generation) is not int
            or not 1 <= generation < 2**31
            or type(language) is not str
            or language not in ("python", "sage")
            or type(kernel_id) is not str
            or len(kernel_id) > 128
            or type(birth_id) is not str
            or re.fullmatch(r"birth-[0-9a-f]{24}", birth_id) is None
        ):
            raise unavailable()
        for name, maximum in (("start_environment", 32), ("start_execution", 128)):
            item = raw.get(name)
            if item is not None and (type(item) is not str or len(item) > maximum):
                raise unavailable()
        epoch = raw.get("start_package_epoch")
        if epoch is not None and (type(epoch) is not int or not 0 <= epoch < 2**62):
            raise unavailable()
        expected_id = (
            "krn-run-"
            + hashlib.sha256(
                json.dumps(
                    {"binding": binding.model_dump(mode="json"), "language": language},
                    sort_keys=True,
                    separators=(",", ":"),
                    ensure_ascii=True,
                ).encode("ascii")
            ).hexdigest()[:32]
        )
        if binding_key != run_kernel_binding_sha256(binding) or kernel_id != expected_id:
            raise unavailable()
        current = self.manager.store.kernel_starts.current(binding.scope.environment_id)
        revision = current[0] if current is not None else None
        info = KernelInfo(
            kernel_id=kernel_id, language=language, generation=generation, current_revision=revision
        )
        start_environment = raw.get("start_environment")
        pin = (
            current is not None
            and current[1] == start_environment
            and self.manager.store.kernel_starts.epoch(
                binding.scope.environment_id,
                binding.incarnation,
                raw.get("start_package_epoch"),
                start_environment,
            )
            == revision
            and (
                (
                    owning_execution is not None
                    and raw.get("start_execution") == owning_execution
                    and fingerprint == start_environment
                )
                or restarted
            )
        )
        birth = KernelBirthPin(
            project_id=binding.scope.project_id,
            environment_id=binding.scope.environment_id,
            session_id=binding.scope.session_id,
            language=language,
            incarnation=binding.incarnation,
            kernel_id=kernel_id,
            sandbox=binding.sandbox,
            sandbox_id=binding.sandbox_id,
            generation=generation,
            birth_id=birth_id,
            start_revision=revision if pin else None,
        )
        return self.state.observe(binding, birth, info, remember=remember)

    async def observe(self, binding: RunKernelBinding) -> RunKernelObservation:
        binding = checked_run_kernel_binding(binding)
        self.proof(binding, allow_closed=True)

        def build(
            context: ExecutionContext, channel: ExecutorChannel, raw: object
        ) -> RunKernelObservation:
            del context
            self.proof(binding, allow_closed=True)
            if type(raw) is not list or len(cast(list[object], raw)) > 2:
                raise unavailable()
            entries: list[KernelLineageEntry] = []
            for item in cast(list[object], raw):
                info = self.map_kernel(binding, item, channel)
                birth = self.state.birth(binding, info.language)
                if (
                    birth is not None
                    and (birth.kernel_id, birth.generation, birth.start_revision)
                    == (info.kernel_id, info.generation, info.start_revision)
                    and info.start_revision is not None
                ):
                    entries.append(
                        KernelLineageEntry(kernel=info, birth=birth, lineage_status="proved")
                    )
                else:
                    entries.append(
                        KernelLineageEntry(
                            kernel=info, lineage_status="unknown", unknown_reason="missing_birth"
                        )
                    )
            current = self.manager.store.kernel_starts.current(binding.scope.environment_id)
            return RunKernelObservation(
                binding=binding,
                current_revision=current[0] if current else None,
                kernels=tuple(entries),
                observed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
            )

        return await self.manager._passive_kernels(
            KernelStatusRequest(context=_context(binding)),
            build,
            operation="run_kernels",
            fields=_wire(binding),
            protocol="run_kernel_protocol",
        )

    async def restart(
        self,
        binding: RunKernelBinding,
        operation_id: str,
        language: Literal["python", "sage"],
        *,
        admitted: Callable[[], bool],
    ) -> RunControlReceipt:
        return await self._control(binding, operation_id, "restart", language, admitted)

    async def close(
        self, binding: RunKernelBinding, operation_id: str, *, admitted: Callable[[], bool]
    ) -> RunControlReceipt:
        return await self._control(binding, operation_id, "close", None, admitted)

    async def _control(
        self,
        binding: RunKernelBinding,
        operation_id: str,
        action: Literal["restart", "close"],
        language: Literal["python", "sage"] | None,
        admitted: Callable[[], bool],
    ) -> RunControlReceipt:
        binding = checked_run_kernel_binding(binding)
        self.admission(admitted)
        key = run_kernel_binding_sha256(binding)
        if len(self._controls) >= 8 or key in self._controls:
            raise unavailable()
        environment, channel = self.proof(binding, allow_closed=action == "close")
        receipt, new = self.state.begin_control(binding, operation_id, action, language)
        if not new:
            return receipt  # pending is unknown, never resend; done is historical only
        observer = self.manager._kernel_observations.get(binding.scope.environment_id)
        if action == "close" and observer is not None:
            observer.valid = False
        withdrawn = False

        async def actual() -> RunControlReceipt:
            environment.requests += 1
            try:
                self.admission(admitted)
                if withdrawn:
                    raise unavailable()
                self.check(binding, environment, channel, allow_closed=action == "close")
                if action == "restart":
                    self.manager.package_admission(binding.scope.environment_id)
                    if not await self.manager._sync_package_gate(
                        binding.scope.environment_id, channel
                    ):
                        raise unavailable()
                    self.manager.package_admission(binding.scope.environment_id)
                    self.check(binding, environment, channel)
                    self.admission(admitted)
                    if withdrawn:
                        raise unavailable()
                reply = await channel.request(
                    "run_" + action,
                    session=binding.scope.session_id,
                    **_wire(binding),
                    **({"language": language} if language is not None else {}),
                    reply_timeout=180,
                )
                self.check(binding, environment, channel, allow_closed=action == "close")
                with self.manager.store._transaction():
                    kernel = (
                        self.map_kernel(
                            binding, reply.get("kernel"), channel, remember=True, restarted=True
                        )
                        if action == "restart"
                        else None
                    )
                    if action == "close" and reply.get("kernels") != []:
                        raise unavailable()
                    return self.state.finish_control(receipt.request, kernel)
            finally:
                environment.requests -= 1
                # Controls are explicit activity; passive reads never use this path.
                environment.last_used = time.monotonic()

        task = asyncio.create_task(actual())
        self._controls[key] = task
        first: asyncio.CancelledError | None = None
        try:
            while not task.done():
                try:
                    await asyncio.shield(task)
                except asyncio.CancelledError as exc:
                    if first is None:
                        first = exc
                    withdrawn = True
            if first is not None:
                # Retrieve any failure without replacing original caller cancellation.
                with contextlib.suppress(BaseException):
                    task.result()
                raise first
            return task.result()
        finally:
            self._controls.pop(key)

    async def drain(self) -> None:
        if self._controls:
            await asyncio.gather(*tuple(self._controls.values()), return_exceptions=True)

    def close_session(self, context: ExecutionContext) -> None:
        """Persist tombstones before guest cleanup; missing namespace is never initialized."""
        db = self.manager.store._db
        if (
            db.execute("SELECT 1 FROM sqlite_master WHERE name='run_dispatch_meta'").fetchone()
            is None
        ):
            return
        rows = db.execute(
            "SELECT CASE WHEN typeof(record)='text' THEN substr(CAST(record AS BLOB),1,4097) END FROM run_kernel_bindings WHERE project=? AND session=? AND environment=? LIMIT 1025",
            (context.project_id, context.session_id, context.environment_id),
        ).fetchall()
        if len(rows) > 1024:
            raise unavailable()
        from sandbox_science.contracts.run_kernels import RunKernelEnrollment

        with self.manager.store._transaction():
            self.state.budget()
            for row in rows:
                enrollment = RunKernelEnrollment.model_validate_json(row[0], strict=True)
                if (
                    enrollment.binding.scope.project_id != context.project_id
                    or enrollment.binding.scope.session_id != context.session_id
                    or enrollment.binding.scope.environment_id != context.environment_id
                ):
                    raise unavailable()
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO run_kernel_closures VALUES(?,?,?)",
                    (
                        run_kernel_binding_sha256(enrollment.binding),
                        context.project_id,
                        datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(),
                    ),
                )
            self.state.budget()

# Internal child-kernel dispatcher

The coherent implementation is in progress on `impl/run-kernel-dispatcher`.
Independent persistence/recovery and executor/lifecycle reviews, final source
freeze, combined gates and real OpenShell acceptance remain pending. This
document describes the intended internal boundary and the current composition;
it does not establish runtime delivery.

The dispatcher extends the [original binding prerequisite](RUN-KERNELS.md) for
[D81](DECISIONS.md). A child uses its canonical session's existing environment
and workspace, with a separate Python or Sage interpreter. It shares the guest
UID and files with MAIN and other children. Interpreter separation provides
neither filesystem isolation nor a security boundary between researchers.

No launcher, delegated model, WorkerClient method, HTTP submission route, model
tool, approval, grant, role profile or concurrency/depth default is added.
Existing whole-session closure still owns all its kernels. Ordinary project
reads of execution records are not a new child-private storage boundary.

## Original selection and admission

The internal `RunCellRequest` has a distinct `run_cell` discriminator, complete
`RunKernelBinding`, ordinary execution context and bounded cell values. It is
absent from the public `ExecutionRequest` union. Its canonical request digest
includes the full original selection. Public `CellRequest` serialization and
its historical defaults/None fields retain their existing bytes and digests.

The binding names the original project, session, environment, parent run,
delegation, child run, managed sandbox, immutable VM ID and daemon incarnation.
A trusted caller derives those values from its actual admitted controller and
original records. A DTO, operation ID, actor, execution ID or logical session
cannot manufacture that authority. Enrollment precedes the first child effect.

Effectful dispatcher calls require an explicit synchronous `admitted` callback.
The caller owns fresh project/session-open/grant checks. The dispatcher also
requires the original already-connected managed channel, retained endpoint,
original enrollment, supported daemon capability and absence of lifecycle,
recovery, recycling or quarantine fences. It rechecks relevant proofs across
awaits and at launch. Callbacks and object comparisons do not prove controller
authentication or an atomic lock across independent control processes.

## One manager and its internal interface

`ExecutionManager` owns one `manager.run_dispatcher`. Borrow that instance;
constructing another dispatcher would create a separate control-task registry
outside the manager's drain. The dispatcher borrows the manager's synchronous
Store connection and existing channel/lifecycle owners.

| Internal method | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `initialize()` | Explicitly create the dispatch namespace once, or validate the existing namespace without resetting it. |
| `submit(request, admitted=...)` | Atomically accept the original child cell and schedule that accepted attempt through existing worker machinery. |
| `get(binding, execution_id, attempt_id)` | Read the exact original selected attempt, retaining its immutable binding. |
| `cancel(binding, execution_id, attempt_id, admitted=...)` | Cancel only that selected original attempt and channel. |
| `restart(binding, operation_id, language, admitted=...)` | Persist a control intent and explicitly restart one child's selected language. |
| `close(binding, operation_id, admitted=...)` | Persist sticky child closure before guest cleanup. |
| `observe(binding)` | Read selected lineage through the existing passive observer lane. |

These interfaces are provisional until the final source freeze. For a fresh
owner, start the ordinary manager, explicitly open the canonical managed session
through a MAIN cell, enroll its original child bindings, then initialize the
dispatch namespace before child submission. For a reopened owner, validate the
existing namespace through the same manager-owned dispatcher before
`manager.start()` recovers retained attempts and endpoints. Fully drain and close
owner1 before owner2 opens those stores. Initialization is not lost-history repair.

## Atomic acceptance and recovery

The worker adds an explicit `executions.kernel_scope` marker. Genuine legacy
rows retain their legacy marker and encoding. Selected child rows use `run-v1`;
their canonical envelope, original digest, attempt/header and selection record
are retained atomically before dispatch. A missing, corrupt, wrong-type,
truncated or contradictory selected marker never enters the MAIN mapper.
Migration must distinguish genuinely old stores from lost selected history.

Separate bounded tables retain selections, generations, births, control receipts
and sticky closures. Reads validate original SQL types and bounded bytes before
UTF-8/JSON parsing, and compare retained canonical columns with their records.
Embedded NUL or coerced text must not normalize into a known marker, digest or
incarnation. Count and logical-byte accounting includes variable scalar fields
and original envelopes before admitting new rows; there is no silent eviction.
These bounds do not measure total SQLite page allocation, RSS or hostile
administrator rewrites of every durable record.

Recovery retains the original accepted request and attempt; it queries/replays
the original daemon journal rather than submitting another command. A healthy
same-incarnation bridge reconnect can preserve the original kernel state.
Missing proof, another daemon incarnation or a replacement VM cannot re-enroll
or attach the old selection to today's kernel. Historical records remain audit
evidence after eligibility disappears.

## Interpreter identity and lineage

The daemon advertises `run_kernel_protocol=1`. Dedicated `run_cell`,
`run_restart`, `run_kernels` and `run_close` operations carry the complete
original binding and its canonical key. Unsupported peers refuse child work.
The executor maintains a separate child-kernel map keyed by project, session,
child run and language; legacy MAIN dictionaries and two-language status DTOs
retain their original namespace.

Child IDs and birth/generation fields receive finite scalar validation before
aggregate encoding. Within the fixed original incarnation, child raw and
normalized generations coincide. Retained generation and birth must agree;
contradictions refuse rather than certify stale lineage. Actual start events
and explicit restart replies may retain an original birth and start-package
pin under existing start/revision transactions. Passive status cannot create a
birth or fill an unknown start revision from today's packages.

The ordinary CP-13/package admission, package epoch, queue/start fences, output
limits, shared-workspace handling and result lifecycle remain in force. The
dispatcher is initially cell-only: no child shell command, background job or
package operation is introduced.

## Cancellation, controls and closing

Public execution-ID cancellation remains legacy-only for selected child
attempts. The dispatcher and existing worker-owned timeout, watchdog, overflow
and recovery paths use an internal exact-selection cancellation path. Fresh
proof must certify the same channel actually used for cancellation; a different
open channel cannot stand in for the original attempt. Corrupt selection is a
refusal, not permission to cancel a MAIN attempt.

Restart/close intents are durable before their RPC. Replay checks the original
operation, action, language, canonical request and selected result identity.
A completed receipt is historical. A pending receipt means the effect is
unknown and is never automatically resent. Lost postreply proof keeps the
pending audit rather than erasing uncertainty or claiming noncommit.

Child close withdraws eligibility before remote cleanup and remains sticky on
failure or caller cancellation. Queued starts/restarts recheck closure at their
actual launch boundary. Closing A drains A's admitted cell/start/control owners
while preserving MAIN and B. Whole-session and daemon close still drain their
complete existing ownership scope.

An admitted control task retains its busy counter, channel and borrowed Store
through timeout/repeated caller cancellation until the actual work settles.
The manager drains its dispatcher before detaching channels or closing Store
owners. Cancellation of an outer future alone does not establish that SQL or a
remote effect stopped.

## Passive observations and acceptance limits

Selected status shares the existing one-per-environment/global-eight observer
lane, close token and total deadline with MAIN observations. It opens no
channel, reconnects no daemon, wakes no stopped VM, refreshes no activity and
consumes no pending state-loss notice. It writes no provisional generation or
birth. Original managed identity is checked after network awaits, including an
empty kernel list. Closure invalidates affected observation ownership.

Root acceptance must freeze the reviewed combined source and helper, run a
bounded pilot, and exercise actual interpreter globals/shared files, exact
cancel/restart/close, same-incarnation reconnect and stopped-VM no-wake behavior.
Gateway proofs must bracket selected reads, and retained endpoint snapshots
must preserve actual normal retirement, including `[]`. Component fault probes
remain distinct from real OpenShell effects. Complete owned teardown and
independent cleanup precede delivery evidence and fresh PR checks.

Even successful runtime acceptance would not prove an authenticated live
delegation controller, delegated model/handback workflow, scientific correctness,
filesystem isolation, monetary accounting, idle wake or successor/replacement
policy. Those remain separate plan items.

# Complete internal child-kernel dispatcher next

Source-only follow-on to signed `c26027e165628d45fff65fad51a24759071d8cd1` (original binding records only). This is a proposed next increment, not implemented behavior or delegated-run delivery. Confirmed D81 is sufficient for separate child interpreters in the existing session; draft depth/concurrency/role/fallback/resume defaults are not adopted.

The next coherent slice should be explicitly internal and initially **cell-only**: submit cell, exact attempt cancel, selected-run restart/status/lineage, and selected-run close. No new launcher/model tool/HTTP selection or child shell/job authority. Unsupported child action kinds must refuse before dispatch. Ordinary MAIN requests continue using the legacy session/language namespace. The future authenticated controller must supply/recheck genuine original run attribution, project/environment/open-session/grants and owned lifetime; the current enrollment cannot establish them.

A durable original selection must be part of accepted request/attempt identity before send, not an optional derived sidecar whose disappearance could turn child work into a legacy cell. Design a distinct internal request marker/envelope and canonical digest that includes the exact original scope/enrollment key and desired language. Persist marker, enrollment reference, request, execution/attempt and dispatch incarnation together. Exact replay may return the original attempt; missing/corrupt selection or changed contents refuses. Preserve legacy request serialized bytes/digests: adding a default-null field to ordinary `CellRequest` can alter historical operation hashes, so that cannot be assumed harmless. Worker recovery must load the original marker and selection, not reconstruct them from actor/current endpoint/result. No deployable worker import of orchestrator DelegationRecords.

Negotiate a distinct daemon run-kernel capability before any accepted child effect. Send a validated exact selection over the already authenticated original daemon channel; no guest-supplied actor/run selector or fallback when the feature is absent. The executor keeps a separate child map keyed project/session/child/language, using the same session directory/environment. Kernel ID derivation must unambiguously include this scope, remain bounded and differ from the legacy kernel ID. Separate interpreter state/processes do not establish filesystem or same-user security isolation.

Use new run-specific generation and birth tables, keyed by complete scope/language, instead of overloading legacy rows. Preserve raw executor generation separately from normalized worker generation, exact original birth ID/start execution/package epoch, and original VM/incarnation. Commit birth/generation/start Execution/event/source cursor atomically. Results retain the exact original start even if that run's kernel is replaced mid-cell. No current package state may fill in an unseen original start. Same-incarnation reconnect can preserve its recorded original identity; changed VM/incarnation initially holds/interruption rather than automatic re-enrollment. Any successor/resume mapping is a separate explicit design, not an inferred draft default.

Cancellation must compare original selected run + exact execution/attempt and channel before sending the existing execution-ID cancel. Restart/close select only that child's kernel; parent/sibling globals and queues survive. Child-only close affects only supported child-cell attempts; no unrelated session job or shell is claimed owned. Session close still stops all child/legacy kernels and existing session jobs. Shared package/CP13 launch gates, true startup ownership and cancellation while queued/starting remain mandatory.

Add a separate <=two-language selected-run status/lineage wrapper, with original enrollment and run scope outside existing KernelInfo. Existing MAIN GUI observation/inbox/hash schema remains unchanged. Use the SAME existing bounded observer lane and session-close token logic, extending token invalidation for exact child close; no extra independent polling capacity. No open/reconnect/wake, last_used/request-count touch, provisional birth write or state_lost consumption on observation. Legacy terminal running_kernels must remain legacy-only; selected-run results get an explicitly typed own-run observation, not an all-runs list squeezed into two languages.

Likely owned seams: new contracts run request/result/observation models; worker executor+daemon capability; manager admission/dispatch/recovery/result/cancel/restart/close and passive mapping; Store original-selection transaction + separate run generation/birth persistence; focused contracts/executor/manager/recovery tests and RUN-KERNELS as-built update. Existing HTTP/WorkerClient/tools/CLI/GUI/control launcher remain unchanged until a separately reviewed trusted consumer exists. Strict public parsing of old endpoints must not accidentally expose an internal request.

Meaningful local fake-kernel/daemon tests: parent+two child globals separate with same workspace; same run/language cells serialize and distinct children do not share queues; one queued/running child cancellation/restart/close preserves siblings; session close stops all; exact same-incarnation restart/reconnect continuity; missing marker/selection/birth, wrong scope/language/VM/incarnation, legacy capability, malformed/oversized copied messages and delayed old replies refuse; managed package hold/race remains fenced; persistence fault/replay cannot ACK uncommitted birth; no-wake status invariants and strict original request-byte compatibility.

Root real OpenShell acceptance later: same shared session/VM, two child kernels with independent globals and expected shared files; actual cancellation/restart plus parent continuity; worker restart reconnect vs new daemon loss separately; CP13 hold and idle passive no-wake. No full delegation claims until actual controller admission/launcher/lifecycle/handback integration and its own acceptance exist.

    'locked': [('locked', ['uv', 'sync', '--locked']),
               ('python-version', ['uv', 'run', '--no-sync', 'python', '--version'])],
    'static': [('format', ['uv', 'run', '--no-sync', 'ruff', 'format', '--check', '.']),

}


def utc():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()


def git(*args):
    return subprocess.check_output(['git', *args], cwd=ROOT, text=True).strip()


def identity(head):
    assert git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == head
    assert git('show', '-s', '--format=%G?', head) == 'G'
    assert not git('status', '--porcelain=v1')
    return git('rev-parse', 'HEAD^{tree}')


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--head', required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--lane', choices=COMMANDS, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--round', default='v1')
    args = parser.parse_args()
    assert re.fullmatch('[0-9a-f]{40}', args.head)

                process = prefix.with_name(prefix.name + '-process.json')

        raw = log.read_bytes()

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Lab33 internal child-kernel acceptance readiness

Source-only design, 2026-10-13. No helper has been activated and no Lab33 state,
service, model, provider, VM, SQL fixture or RPC has been created by this review.
The dispatcher is WIP. Its eventual signed source, combined gates, actual-main
integration, exact API and independent review must precede executable-helper
review and root-owned runtime admission.

## Ownership and authority

Use one disposable in-process production `ExecutionManager`/worker `Store` and
`RunKernelDispatcher`. The ordinary worker HTTP service is absent/stopped for
this fixture; two managers must never own the same environment, SQLite connection
or daemon channel. The dispatcher author confirmed this arrangement is feasible.
Root owns normal lab infrastructure, canonical environment creation, original VM
receipt, fixed driver stages, every cell/control effect and final teardown.

The driver uses actual `OpenShellBackend`, `Environments`, production manager
configuration and ordinary package/CP-13/shared-workspace checks. Reuse the actual
CLI assembly seams rather than a fake backend/channel, a local-dev fallback or a
second ad-hoc worker. Root creates the environment once through the canonical
production environment API/component, records its exact creation scope/profile/
policy/name/immutable ID and closes that setup owner before the sole manager starts.
No install is needed: the fixed cells use Python's standard library only.

Create fresh marked 0700 `lab33` state and actual canonical `ProjectStore` and
`DocumentStore` records. Take the project's real shared environment ID and one
open session from `ProjectStore`; do not rewrite its binding. Keep a root-generated
synthetic parent-run ID in the fixture manifest. Two actual
`DelegationRecords.prepare(ParentAuthority(...), fixed_operation, fixed_brief)`
transactions generate the original delegation and child-run IDs. Retain their
exact receipts before enrollment. No execution ID, actor, session ID, manually
invented child ID or claimed model run substitutes for those generated IDs.

This is a deliberately synthetic host-control fixture using real records and real
worker/daemon execution. It proves neither an authenticated live controller nor
a delegated model/launcher/handback workflow. A fixture admission callback can
freshly compare exact project/session/environment, open control lifetime,
original prepared receipt and allowed fixed stage. New sessions already have a
control-owned `kernel_notice_lifetime`; compare it privately without putting it
in guest messages or public evidence. This callback is not production authentication,
a resource grant, a controller security proof or an atomic cross-process lock.

## Interface pins needed before a helper is written

Current proposed internal API from the author, not frozen signatures:

| Seam | Proposed interface / dependency |
| --- | --- |
| Initialization | `RunKernelDispatcher(manager)` and explicit `initialize()`; recover existing namespace without resetting it. |
| Original enrollment | Existing `manager.enroll_run_kernel(scope, operation_id, initialize=...)`, after an ordinary MAIN cell opens the canonical managed session. |
| Child cell | `submit(RunCellRequest, admitted=callback) -> (RunCellExecution, created)`. |
| Original attempt | `get(binding, execution_id, attempt_id)` and `cancel(binding, execution_id, attempt_id, admitted=...)`. |
| Child control | `restart(binding, operation_id, language, admitted=...)` and `close(binding, operation_id, admitted=...)`. |
| Passive selection | `observe(binding)` using the existing manager observer lane, not a new polling quota. |
| Reconnect | Exact startup/initialization order, selected recovery loader, daemon detach behavior and ownership of wait/event tasks still need the frozen implementation. |

Freeze exact source/schema/control receipts, terminal states, safe wait/get
selection, package-epoch/start/birth pins and unknown/closed outcomes first.
The current worker source branch starts from binding c260 and does not yet contain
the delegation module; the eventual helper needs the reviewed combined product,
not that incomplete author checkout. Public `ExecutionRequest`/`WorkerClient`,
HTTP routes, ordinary kernel DTOs and model tools remain unchanged.

## Bounded stages and expected evidence

First run a small pilot: parent plus child A and child B each assign a different
fixed integer to the same variable, print only bounded expected scalar fields,
and report their kernel/process identities. Compare exact scope and original
VM/incarnation for all three. Distinct interpreter globals and guest process IDs
are the intended result; shared UID/filesystem is not security isolation.

Then admit only these fixed stages. Suggested engineering caps are at most20
fixed Python cells,8 child controls,1 session close,512 source bytes/cell,1KiB
expected output/cell,finite per-cell deadlines and one finite driver deadline.
These are helper limits to finalize after the pilot, not new product defaults.
No arbitrary command/code/model/selector/config/URL input is accepted.

| Stage | Required proof / honest failure boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Parent + A + B | Same canonical session, environment, cwd/workspace and original managed VM/incarnation; independent globals and distinct child kernel/birth keys. Legacy MAIN listing stays legacy-only. |
| Shared workspace | A exclusively writes one fixed relative fixture file. B and parent read its exact fixed bytes in their own interpreters. Shared files remain shared after A restart. |
| Exact attempt cancellation | Wait for actual selected start evidence, then cancel the original A execution/attempt. B and parent continue and retain globals. Wrong child/attempt refuses without canceling another execution. If queued cancellation is observable, add one queued A attempt and prove it never starts; label it component-only otherwise. |
| Restart A | Persist the original fixed control intent/receipt. A loses its global and has a new generation/birth; parent/B globals, generations and birth pins remain exact. A repeated exact committed receipt is historical, not permission to repeat an unknown RPC. |
| Bridge/manager reconnect | Detach and fully drain owner1 before owner2 opens the same Store/daemon. Require exact original VM and daemon incarnation, kernel IDs, raw/normalized generations and birth/start pins before/after. Read back globals only after passive continuity proof. No command is automatically resubmitted. |
| Close A | Exact child-only close withdraws A eligibility and stops only its kernels/owned cell attempts. A new submit refuses; B and parent remain usable. Do not claim unrelated shell/jobs were owned by A. |
| Passive stopped phase | Root uses the normal idle-release/suspension path and exports fresh exact-original-VM Stopped proofs before/after30 finite selected reads. No reconnect, activity refresh, birth/generation writes, state-lost consumption or SQL mutation; unavailable/held is a valid result, not healthy-empty. |
| Original incarnation loss | A separately admitted harmless MAIN resume may create a new daemon incarnation. Original B binding must hold/refuse, not silently re-enroll, attach to a new kernel or repeat an attempt. Keep the old audit intact. |
| Original VM loss/replacement | Prefer a terminal explicit root-owned loss phase after other proofs: remove the exact owned original VM and verify original selections refuse before child effects. If root also admits a replacement, track both VM identities and prove old selections never rebind. Without this actual phase, report VM replacement only as reviewed component coverage; do not equate it with bridge reconnect or incarnation change. |
| Session close | Before final loss or in a separately ordered fixed phase, actual session close stops the remaining legacy/child kernels and invalidates pending selected reads. Its ordinary lifecycle semantics remain primary. No subsequent successful cell is needed to test closure. |

The precise order of terminal session-close and VM-loss phases must be settled
against the frozen implementation. Never reopen/reseed a closed child or erase a
run namespace just to keep later cases convenient. A small second canonical
prestarted scope is preferable if those destructive boundaries otherwise
interfere; it must be declared and budgeted before admission.

## Stopped endpoints, chronology and unknown effects

Normal idle retirement may delete `executor_endpoints`. Current stopped snapshots
must export actual `[]`, not reconstruct a present endpoint from history. Any
helper-only allowance requires the exact previously accepted before/after
original binding, current typed stopped environment with the same original
name/UUID, and fresh phase/run/head/helper-bound exact-original-VM Stopped proof.
The old incarnation is historical only. Missing endpoints in first-read/ready,
foreign/deleted/unproved state or mismatched original identity refuse.

Both gateway proofs must temporally bracket all selected reads. Normalize full
allowlisted SQL rows losslessly through strict JSON before persistence/comparison,
including order, types and every scalar; no tuple/list false equality failure,
subset comparison, replacement columns or nonfinite values. Retain held read-only
DB/row ownership and close every inspection connection. Do not load unbounded
worker records/blobs to build a snapshot.

Each new effect has an exclusive run/stage-bound intent before admission and an
exact immutable receipt afterward. Intent without receipt is unknown: query the
original accepted attempt/control and inspect preserved evidence; do not issue a
new operation, replay mutable intent, reset state or infer noncommit. First-fail,
late reply, repeated cancellation and lost-control-ACK fault injection belong to
isolated host/component fixtures unless an explicit safe real-runtime hook is
reviewed. Source/fault tests must not be labeled actual OpenShell effects.

## Admission, outputs and teardown

Root's public admission binds one final signed clean head, helper SHA, input/build
pins, fresh marker/run ID, canonical project/session/environment, expected original
VM identity and finite stages. Private configuration/auth stays0600 and in memory;
no raw provider/gateway/config/token/URL, credential fingerprint, arbitrary output,
exception, model text or full settings hash is exported. A public metadata admission
is distinct from a private auth file, regardless of its filesystem mode.

Public receipts use explicit schemas/size/count caps and allowlisted fixed cell
results only: source/run/stage/scope, generated delegation/child IDs, operation/
execution/attempt IDs, canonical request/binding keys, terminal/control outcome,
kernel/birth/generation/start/current pins and safe time/identity fields. Label
synthetic control records, real daemon/VM evidence and component fault tests
separately. Original failures remain immutable; corrections get separate source
and result pins. No old-helper PASS or corrected-helper runtime claim by inference.

One owner retains every task/channel/Store/descriptor through timeout, repeated
cancellation and shutdown. Drain before closing borrowed stores, then close
manager/channels/backend/environment/control owners in the frozen API's actual
order. Root tears down the exact owned environment(s), units, process-start
identities, ports and private/provider files metadata-only; no unrelated state or
old private raw logs are read/hashed. Independent cleanup checks use known paths,
PIDs/start identities, listener metadata, root public original-VM removal evidence
and any actually owned browser IDs only. This internal-only fixture requires no
browser or provider/model registration for its own acceptance.

## Coverage and remaining gaps

Real runtime can establish separate Python interpreter globals, shared workspace,
actual exact cancellation/restart/close behavior, same-incarnation reconnect and
selected no-wake/old-binding refusal. Existing/fresh CP-13 fake/component gates
remain useful if no provisioning is needed, but do not become actual Lab33 hold,
package installation, permission or policy-race acceptance. Python-only runtime
establishes no positive Sage case.

Even a successful Lab33 proves no authenticated live delegation controller,
launcher/model role/fallback/approval defaults, handback delivery/save/ACK,
spend/concurrency policy, filesystem isolation or scientific correctness. Source
readiness remains blocked on final dispatcher API/source/gates, owned construction/
reconnect order and independently reviewed helper/admission. No current issue
requires activating a speculative effectful helper now.

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
# Lab33 helper author plan

Source-only preparation; no application/helper main, live SQL, worker/daemon RPC,
services, provider, model, VM or research kernel has been activated by the author.
The helper checkout stays clean until root repins the N3-corrected product union.

Default is stdlib describe-only. Effectful fixed stages require a literal reviewed
admission switch, a fresh owned non-symlink lab marker, root-specified exact signed
clean HEAD and fixed production input hashes before lazy application imports.
Settings are bounded private in-memory input from the fixed owned lab path; no
configuration/token/lifetime values or fingerprints, arbitrary outputs or raw
exceptions enter public evidence. No URL/path/project/environment/code selector.

Use one production manager.run_dispatcher. Reuse exact CLI Environments,
OpenShellBackend (refuse LocalBackend), Store/Blobs/SharedSync/Provisioner and hooks;
create_app + AppRunner.setup/cleanup installs normal lifecycle hooks WITHOUT a
TCPSite/listener or HTTP client. Close/drain runner, provisioner, manager and each
borrowed Store/records owner in production order. No background suspender/watcher.
All admitted tasks remain owned through repeated cancellation and final cleanup.

Proposed fixed stages: init (canonical project, two shared-environment sessions,
three DelegationRecords.prepare identities and one managed environment intent),
pilot (MAIN/A/B), flows (shared file, exact started cancel, A restart and B/MAIN
preservation), reconnect (owner1 drained before owner2; same-incarnation passive
identity proof before three fixed global reads), close (sticky A close/refusal,
B/MAIN preservation), session (session2 MAIN+C, close session1, C preservation),
suspend (explicit normal Environments.suspend after measured idle), stopped
(read-only30 selected reads, exact retired endpoint[] and unchanged bounded SQL
between fresh root-owned original-VM Stopped projections), resume (one explicit
harmless MAIN session2 call; original C refuses under new incarnation), loss
(read-only original-selection refusal after root-owned exact original VM deletion),
inspect (bounded historical canonical receipts only). Stage splitting/order will be
mechanically pinned; unknown intent blocks new effects instead of auto-retry.

The19 fixed Python cells use only bounded synthetic integers/PIDs and one fixed
shared fixture file, <=512bytes source and <=1KiB expected output each. Budget
caps20 cells,8 child controls,1session close,1 managed VM and finite per-call/driver
admission. Every effect gets an exclusive fsynced intent before dispatch and exact
immutable receipt afterward. A receipt is matched to original scope/binding/
request/operation/execution/attempt, not reconstructed from a later current view.
Synthetic admitted callback freshly compares actual original project/session/open
lifetime and prepared child records; it proves fixture consistency, no live caller
authentication/model/launcher/grant/handback/security-isolation claim.

Prefer fixed root-generated safe gateway projections over helper access to raw
CLI annotations/auth. Require exact run/head/helper/phase and original VM name+ID,
aware dated chronology before/after all stopped reads. Export only actual typed
allowlisted SQL columns/bytes, preserving tuples losslessly as JSON lists. All
read-only DB/file descriptors close; no endpoint backfill or provisional birth.

Author validation is AST/stdlib/fake-component guards and scoped format/type only.
Root owns exact helper adoption, independent review, source gates, any activation,
VM/provider/lab setup, real effects, public evidence export and full teardown.
